conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be your doctor during this stay. Can you tell me about what brought you in today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi. I’ve had this pain in my upper belly for two days now. It’s the same kind I get with my pancreatitis—fullness, radiating to my back. I’ve been nauseous and throwing up, haven’t kept anything down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Any fever, cough, or urinary symptoms?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, no fever or anything like that. Just the pain and nausea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Got it. We know you have chronic pancreatitis from your CF gene mutation, and you usually don’t have high lipase during flares. We’ll treat this as an acute flare. We’ve started IV fluids and Dilaudid for pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. That last dose already helped a little.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We checked your labs. Your lipase is 50, which is normal, but that fits your history. Liver enzymes are a bit high, but not alarming. We’ll keep you NPO for now and give nutrition through the IV.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Makes sense. I usually can’t eat during these flares.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How’s the pain today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Still there, but better than yesterday. Still nauseous though.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep the IV anti-nausea meds going. Also, you mentioned a headache—any idea what kind it is?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Feels like my usual migraines. I’ve taken Fioricet before, even when I’m NPO.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay, we’ll give you Fioricet every four hours as needed. We’ll also keep monitoring your heart with EKGs since you’re on Seroquel and amitriptyline.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Wait, is that because of the long QT issue last time?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Your QTc was 440 on admission—within normal, but we’re cautious. We’ll recheck it after restarting your meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your pain is improving. We’re going to try advancing your diet to clear liquids today if you’re up for it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. I’d love to try something small.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll start slow. Also, we’re restarting your home meds—Lisinopril, amlodipine, omeprazole, and Lamictal—since you’re tolerating PO.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And Seroquel and amitriptyline?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll restart those today too, but we’ll monitor your EKG closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. We’re switching from IV Dilaudid to your oral tramadol for pain control.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. I prefer the tramadol anyway.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Also, we noticed a sore on your lower gum. Is that from biting it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I must’ve bitten it when I was dry heaving. It’s pretty painful.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll give you lidocaine viscous mouthwash to use before meals to help with the pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re ordering a CT scan today to make sure there’s no pseudocyst or blockage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Last time it was clear, so I hope this is too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The CT came back. No pseudocyst, no obstruction, no mass. Your pancreas looks normal. The colon has some changes from old colitis, but nothing new.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. So it’s just the flare?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. We’re confident it’s acute on chronic pancreatitis. We’ll keep advancing your diet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re going to place a midline in your right arm today. Your veins have been tough to access, and this will help with fluids and meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that like a PICC line?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Similar, but shorter and doesn’t go as far. It’s safer given your history of clots in the left arm.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The midline was placed successfully in your right brachial vein. It’s working well, and you’re already getting fluids through it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I hope this helps avoid more needle sticks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve been reviewing your labs. Your hemoglobin is low at 9.1, but it’s stable for you. It’s normocytic, and iron studies are normal, so it’s likely chronic underproduction.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So no transfusion needed?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not at this time. It’s not causing symptoms, and you’re not actively bleeding.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Also, your EKG today shows QTc of 449. It’s slightly up from admission, but still not prolonged. We’ll follow up with your PCP to check it again soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Should I stop Seroquel?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, we’ll keep it for now. But your PCP will need to check your heart function and possibly do an echo.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing really well. You’re eating regular food, pain is controlled with oral meds, and you’re moving around fine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I can go home soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, likely tomorrow. We’ll discharge you on your regular meds, including tramadol, Creon, and your psychiatric medications.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about the mouth sore?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Keep using the lidocaine rinse. See your dentist or PCP if it doesn’t heal in a week or two.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the weight check you mentioned?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, weigh yourself daily. If you gain more than three pounds, call your doctor—could be fluid buildup.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Any restrictions?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No heavy lifting with your right arm for a few days because of the midline. Otherwise, resume normal activities as tolerated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—you’re cleared to go home today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What’s the plan after discharge?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Continue all your medications as prescribed. Follow up with your PCP in a week, especially for the EKG to check your QTc.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my pain specialist?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, follow up with Dr. ___ for pain management. Same for your psychiatrist and neurologist.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been through a lot, but I feel much better now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done really well. We’re confident you’ll continue to improve at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you for taking care of me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Call us if symptoms return or if you have any concerns.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Have a good day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You too. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a quick update—your discharge papers are ready. You’ll get prescriptions for all your meds, including Creon and tramadol.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. I’ll make sure to pick them up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Also, keep using the lidocaine rinse for the mouth ulcer until it heals.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do. Any diet changes?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Low-fat diet as usual. Small, frequent meals. Avoid alcohol completely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know the drill. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re all set. We’ll see you in follow-up if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Appreciate it. I’m ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll have the discharge team get you ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. Thanks for everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care and feel better soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—your midline will be removed at your follow-up if it’s no longer needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll let them know.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: And keep monitoring your weight and symptoms.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I’ve learned my triggers.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s good to hear. Stay in touch with your care team.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re very welcome. Have a safe trip home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You too. We’re here if you need us.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I appreciate that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All set. The nurse will assist you with discharge paperwork.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Get some rest.
